solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: To run slow recording takes (6)

indicators.note: the recording takes the other piece in, holding it inside

blocks.note: CD = compact disc, a recording; it opens around the next piece
a clock that runs slow loses time

annotation.surface: A film crew grinding through slow, repetitive recording takes.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'To', as in a door pulled to: shut. 'Run slow' is a clock's failing, so LOSE, not a jogger.
annotation.definitionFit: A door that is to has been pushed shut, so it is closed.

entries.clue: Plain figures in rollover of National Lottery (5)

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the following words
the letters are rolled over, read backwards

annotation.surface: A plain lottery statistic: the numbers in a rollover draw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rollover' is a real lottery term for an unwon jackpot carried forward, which is why the reversal indicator hides so well here.
annotation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy treeless plain in South America.

entries.clue: Fine quality woman is protecting seabirds (9)

indicators.note: the woman's phrase wraps round the birds to guard them

blocks.note: SHE'S = woman is; it splits after SHE

annotation.surface: A fine woman shielding seabirds from harm.
annotation.walkthrough: The erne, or sea eagle, is a crossword regular. Note where the protecting phrase breaks open: between its E and its final S.
annotation.definitionFit: Sheerness is the fineness of a thin, see-through fabric.

entries.clue: One of 28 days threatening to boycott Trump and co? (6)

indicators.note: the second word stays away from the first, so its letters are dropped

blocks.note: Trump's administration is the US government; removed from OMINOUS

annotation.surface: A bad month or so of threats to boycott the Trump administration.
annotation.walkthrough: '28 days' looks like February, but the definition stops at 28: a standard double-six domino set has 28 pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A standard double-six set has 28 dominoes, so a domino is one of 28.

entries.clue: Lives so devastated after daughters break up (8)

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt
the anagram comes after the D

annotation.surface: A family devastated when the daughters split up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a family break-up; the definition sits at the far end and is a verb, not a description of the daughters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean bringing a partnership or meeting to an end.

entries.clue: “Visit Again Soon!”: National Trust boards mimic animal park officer (4,2,1,8)

indicators.note: the National Trust climbs aboard, getting inside the rest

blocks.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
NT = National Trust, the British heritage charity

annotation.surface: A National Trust sign bidding visitors farewell while staff impersonate a zoo keeper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Animal park officer' looks like one job title but breaks into two words, and 'mimic' is a verb in its impersonating sense.
annotation.definitionFit: “Don't be a stranger” is a friendly way of asking someone to come back soon.

entries.clue: Earl cutting key to open small window (8)

indicators.note: the Earl is cut out of the key
the shortened key prises open the word for small and sits inside it

annotation.surface: An earl cutting a key to get into a house through a small window.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small window' wants to be the definition, but 'small' is SLIGHT and the definition is just 'window'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: this is the particular window set into a roof or ceiling.

entries.clue: Working interminably tedious bar is initially given unwanted exposure (5)

indicators.note: the remaining letters are set to work in a new order
without its end: the last letter goes
leave out, as in 'all bar one'
take only the first letter of 'is'

blocks.note: remove I, the first letter of 'is', leaving TEDOU

annotation.surface: A dull bar job, and the worker gets publicly exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: Two cuts come before the shuffle: the end of 'tedious', then its I.
annotation.definitionFit: To be outed is to have something private, usually one's sexuality, revealed against one's wishes.

entries.clue: Farewell can move ultimately, with note found inside card (9)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'move'
the note sits in the middle of the rest

annotation.surface: A goodbye note tucked inside a card, telling someone to move on.
annotation.walkthrough: Latin farewells are fair game, as in 'ave atque vale'. 'Move ultimately' reads as a verb phrase but gives only one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A valentine is the card sent on St Valentine's Day.

entries.clue: Remuneration comprises a million, one notes (5,5)

indicators.note: the pay holds the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: pay = remuneration; it splits after PA
a = per, as in £5 a day

annotation.surface: A pay packet that adds up to a million, in notes.
annotation.walkthrough: The small word 'a' is the key: it means PER.
annotation.definitionFit: Notes means banknotes, the printed form of cash as opposed to coins.

entries.clue: Small deserts for all that work (4)

indicators.note: the S walks out of the word

annotation.surface: Small rewards for all that work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' reads as the noun (just deserts), but it is the verb: S deserts STILL.
annotation.definitionFit: To till land is to work it, ploughing it for crops.

entries.clue: Send over cross, then thump opener (8)

indicators.note: each word is sent over, turned back to front
puts the thump straight after the cross

blocks.note: rood = a cross, as in a church's rood screen

annotation.surface: A football match: send the cross over, then thump the first goal.
annotation.walkthrough: The football words (cross, opener) are a disguise. Both pieces are turned round separately, not the whole string.
annotation.definitionFit: You turn a doorknob to open a door, so it is an opener.

entries.clue: I eat by what looks like ten (6)

indicators.note: the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: the letters I and O look like the digits 1 and 0

annotation.surface: Someone eating beside a number ten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the definition: I is the chemical symbol for iodine.
annotation.definitionFit: I is iodine's symbol in the periodic table.

entries.clue: Prime locations for cherries … this one? (4)

definitions.text: Prime locations for cherries … this one?

indicators.note: take the letters at prime-numbered positions: 2, 3, 5 and 7

annotation.surface: A question about where the best cherries grow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime' reads as top-quality, but it is the maths sense: prime-numbered positions. And where are those letters? Right here, in this clue.
annotation.definitionFit: The letters sit right here, so the clue answers its own question.

entries.clue: Focus is what’s under this impressive dish, finally lifted (9)

indicators.note: the final letter is lifted off

annotation.surface: A cook presenting an impressive dish with a lid lifted to show what's underneath.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is geology: an earthquake starts at its focus underground, and the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above.
annotation.definitionFit: An earthquake's focus lies directly under its epicentre.

entries.clue: Fit shelves at intervals in loft (8)

indicators.note: things spaced at intervals have gaps between them, so read every other letter and skip the gaps
those letters go inside the loft

blocks.note: attic = loft; it splits after AT

annotation.surface: Someone putting up shelves at intervals in the attic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit shelves' is DIY, but 'Fit' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone in good physical shape is described by either word.

entries.clue: Space to operate weapon that shoots Australian native in tree (5,4)

indicators.note: the weapon and the animal go inside the tree

blocks.note: an elm; it splits after EL

annotation.surface: A hunter needing room to aim at an Australian animal up a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' sounds like a person, but it is the kangaroo.
annotation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move or act freely.

entries.clue: Odd threesome in the bed adopting equally loopy bedroom appliance (8)

indicators.note: take three odd-numbered letters
those letters take the rest in

blocks.note: ThEbEd: letters 1, 3 and 5; splits after TE

annotation.surface: A saucy picture of a threesome in bed with somebody loopy.
annotation.walkthrough: A Teasmade is a British bedside machine that brews tea with an alarm clock. The racy surface hides a very tame appliance.
annotation.definitionFit: A Teasmade is a bedside appliance that makes tea to wake you.

entries.clue: Hide behind young woman [as] neccessary? (8)

indicators.note: the hide comes after the young woman

annotation.surface: Someone hiding behind a young woman when they have to.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: NECCESSARY is wrongly spelt, with a double C. The typo is deliberate.
annotation.definitionFit: “Neccessary” is how necessary looks when misspelt.

entries.clue: Probable second option if (a) is no extras (4)

blocks.note: on a two-option form, if (a) is no then (b) is the opposite
surface hedging: (b) is only probably the other answer

annotation.surface: A multiple-choice form with options (a) and (b).
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are extras: runs scored when the ball passes the batter and the wicketkeeper without being hit.
annotation.definitionFit: Byes are one kind of extra in cricket, runs not credited to a batter.

entries.clue: Made a copy of 1 with a different partner (6)

indicators.note: in bridge N and S are partners, so the S is swapped for N

blocks.note: S replaced by its bridge partner N

annotation.surface: Copying someone with a new partner in tow.
annotation.walkthrough: North and South partner each other at bridge, so S gives way to N.
annotation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make an exact copy of it.

entries.clue: Court action reversed in the end, defendants in clear (6)

indicators.note: the assembled pieces are read backwards
take the end of 'defendants'

blocks.note: net = clear, as in clear profit

annotation.surface: A legal case overturned in the end, with the defendants cleared.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface points at a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by setting: the court is a sports court, and the action on it is the game played there.

entries.clue: Not at the outset aware of dress fabric (5)

indicators.note: take only the first letter

blocks.note: IN ON = party to a secret, aware of it

annotation.surface: Someone unaware of the fabric their dress is made of.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not at the outset' reads as 'not at first', but it only supplies N.
annotation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer silk or chiffon fabric used for dresses.

entries.clue: No one on the credit side making concessions? (8)

definitions.text: No one on the credit side

blocks.clueFragment: No one on the credit side
blocks.note: split into two words: everybody in debt, nobody in credit

annotation.surface: A negotiation where everybody is in the red and giving ground.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ALL OWING and nobody is in credit.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: making concessions means granting or permitting, and as two words the answer says everyone owes money.

entries.clue: Outfits playing on diamonds contributing to fashion, in essence (5)

indicators.note: the words contribute the answer's letters

annotation.surface: Clothes and diamonds contributing to the essence of high fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: The diamonds are baseball diamonds, and a nine is a baseball team. The fashion words also echo 'dressed to the nines', but that is only surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A baseball team fields nine players, so teams are called nines.

entries.clue: One at last bound for New College (4)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'at'
make the letters new, rearranging them

annotation.surface: A student at last heading off to New College, Oxford.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New College' looks like one name, the Oxford college, but 'New' is the anagram indicator and 'College' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Eton College is the English public school near Windsor.

entries.clue: Putting on a motley on pain of death? (2,8)

indicators.note: a motley is a jumbled mix, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A jester forced to put on his motley costume or die.
annotation.walkthrough: Motley is a jester's costume, so 'putting on a motley' reads as dressing up.
annotation.definitionFit: Being held at gunpoint means complying or being shot.

entries.clue: Dancer perhaps announced time for queen and honey? (8)

indicators.note: spoken, so the sounds count, not the spellings

blocks.note: a queen's time on the throne is her reign
honey and dear are both endearments

annotation.surface: A royal announcing it is time for tea and honey.
annotation.walkthrough: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer, with Dasher and Prancer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Dancer is one of the team that pulls Santa's sleigh.

entries.clue: Red Putin’s agreed to conceal (6)

annotation.surface: Russia's president agreeing to hide something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red' feels like a political label beside Putin, but it is the colour: damask is a deep pink-red.
annotation.definitionFit: Damask is a pinkish-red colour, like the damask rose.
